score = interp/3 x measurability; measurability = best arm's min partner reliability x ceiling factor

entries.title: Euclidean against Canberra distance: gain-invariant agreement

invariance holds on z-scored data only: normal-scoring breaks it (shared gain -.061)
a gain over an unscaled noise floor changes SNR with amplitude, so it counts as amplitude-dependent correlation
sign-disagreement samples score 1 whatever their amplitude, so near-zero samples weigh heavily

guide_proposals: Static-statistic principle: on z-scored channels the expectation of any time-exchangeable bivariate statistic (rank correlations, MI estimators, dCor, IDS, L1/L2/Canberra distances, barycentre moments) under a Gaussian process is a fixed function of r. Any pair from that set is therefore a principled non-minimal pair beyond IAAFT, and its reading is the feature the more flexible statistic weights. Maxima (Chebyshev, barycentre max) are the exception: their expectation also depends on T and the spectrum of x -+ y, which joint IAAFT fixes.

Classes with no entry in assumptions.READINGS: chebyshev vs cityblock (axis screen), canberra vs euclidean/cosine (gain-invariant agreement on z-scored data), aggregation mean vs max for bary-sq (joint extreme co-excursion).
Envelope correlation: under Gaussianity its partner is |gamma|^2 = r^2 + corr(x, H[y])^2, not r^2; z(pec, r^2) mixes in lag.

Remove saturation from z0 by mapping the Gaussian-determined partner through the known relation (arcsin for ranks, Thm 7 for dCor, -1/2 log for MI, closed envelope forms) before correlating; z0 is then 1 minus estimator noise under the null.
Canberra gain invariance holds on z-scored, not normal-scored, windows; a normal-scored IAAFT construction removes it.

SPIs unbundled upstream as exact affine functions of a kept SPI (pdist_cosine, bary-sq_euclidean_mean, the shrinkage covariances) give exactly the z of the kept SPI, because z is a Pearson correlation of edge profiles; read and name such pairs through the kept SPI.

Ceiling rule for mapped pairs: when the Gaussian-determined partner is mapped through its exact relation, z0 is 1 minus estimator noise by construction, so z0 > .98 excludes the best-mapped pairs (xi_g|xi z0 .980 excluded while mi_g|xi, a cruder map of the same contrast, passes). For mapped pairs, judge informativeness by the null SD of the net, not by z0.

upstream.principle: z is the Pearson correlation of two edge profiles (assumptions.py), so an SPI that is an exact affine function of a kept SPI gives exactly the same z with any partner: pdist_cosine = 1 - r, bary-sq_euclidean_mean = (1 + r)/2, cov_{LedoitWolf,OAS,ShrunkCovariance} = (1 - delta) r with one delta per window on z-scored data, and their cov-sq forms. A monotone nonlinear function (pdist_euclidean = sqrt(2T(1 - r)), lmfit of r^2, ppc of PLV) changes z only through curvature, which the catalogue already treats as an identity or saturation control, and the mapped-partner convention uses the analytic form. Kendall is not an exact function of Spearman (the relation depends on the copula), but its residual was already excluded as a near-ceiling diagnostic. So the merged cuts remove no reading; they agree with the identity, shrinkage, kendall-spearman and debias exclusions.
